verifiedFacts.claim: Iggy Pop wrote that he asked Ron Asheton to begin “T.V. Eye” in the style of John Lee Hooker, playing single notes against a one-string drone before building to full sonics.

sourceRefs.label: Iggy and the Stooges
sourceRefs.title: 'Building Fun House' by Iggy Pop
sourceRefs.extract: T.V. Eye was the key number on the record for me. To get that, I had to camp in the hallway outside Ron’s door for over an hour pounding and pleading with him to let me come in and write a god damn song. He finally compromised by coming out into the hallway with his Fender Princeton practice amp and his Strat and played me the riff. I thought, “oh shit that’s really got it!” but the way he was playing it, in the style of “No Fun” or “I Wanna Be Your Dog” from our first record sounded too large and thick to allow the song to go anywhere. So I asked him to throw in a variation for my tag line, and to begin the number in the style of John Lee Hooker, an artist we both liked, playing the single notes against a one string drone, blues style, before letting it build up to full sonics.

verifiedFacts.claim: Steve Mackay said “L.A. Blues” developed from the band’s freeform “Hippy or Freakout” concert ending, which producer Don Gallucci suggested making into its own track and which they recorded live in the studio.

sourceRefs.label: Galway Advertiser (archived by Cult of Estel)
sourceRefs.title: Steve Mackay – Sax Man, talks The Stooges, Iggy and ESTEL.
sourceRefs.extract: However the album’s most uncompromising track is the ‘free jazz’ of ‘LA Blues’, which these days Iggy describes as something akin to “a demonic howl”. “As a finale to our shows we would do what we called a Hippy or Freakout ending in freeform, leaving guitar and bass feeding back as we left the stage while the crowd was still passing Jim around [after one of his stagedives],” says Steve. “Don Galucci, the producer, thought it would be good to make it its own track. We did it all live in the studio.
